title: Trump: The Apprentice, created by Putin collaborator, premieres on NBC
description_short: Trump: The Apprentice, created by Putin collaborator, premieres on NBC
description_medium: The Apprentice, produced by Mark Burnett and starring Donald Trump, premiered on NBC in January 2004. A separate account says Burnett discussed a Russia-focused reality project, Destination: Mir, and said Vladimir Putin was involved in that proposal. The sources do not establish Putin’s role in creating The Apprentice or NBC’s decision to cast Trump.
description_long: The Apprentice premiered on NBC in January 2004, with Donald Trump as its host and Mark Burnett as producer. The materials supplied for this entry connect Burnett to a separate project he pursued before the series: Destination: Mir, a proposed reality competition associated with Russia’s Mir space station. The linked account quotes Burnett saying “Putin is involved” in the negotiations around that concept. Destination: Mir did not become The Apprentice. Burnett’s work on both ideas links the projects through their producer, but the supplied sources do not show that Vladimir Putin collaborated on The Apprentice, influenced its creation or affected NBC’s choice of Trump as host. A later appointment of former Breitbart chair Stephen Bannon as Trump’s chief strategist establishes a separate political connection to Breitbart, not Putin’s involvement in the television series. The premiere can be recorded as a television event; the claim that it was created by a Putin collaborator needs a source specific to The Apprentice.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: The Apprentice, created by Putin collaborator, premieres on NBC
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: The Apprentice, created by Putin collaborator, premieres on NBC

notes: Needs context: the supplied passage links Putin to Burnett’s separate, unrealized Destination: Mir project, not to The Apprentice. Proposed correction: describe the January 2004 premiere and report the Russia-project connection separately.

title: Trump: Right-wing website Breitbart is launched in Israel
description_short: Trump: Right-wing website Breitbart is launched in Israel
description_medium: Jewish Telegraphic Agency reporting places the launch of Breitbart Jerusalem in November 2015, not January 2007. It describes a 2007 Israel trip by founder Andrew Breitbart and CEO Larry Solov as the setting where they discussed the parent Breitbart News Network. The chronology appears to conflate that trip with the later launch of the Israel-focused site.
description_long: Jewish Telegraphic Agency reported that Breitbart Jerusalem marked its first anniversary in November 2016, placing the site’s launch in November 2015. CEO Larry Solov said he and founder Andrew Breitbart discussed creating a new media company during a 2007 trip to Jerusalem. The 2007 trip is therefore part of the parent network’s origin story, not the launch date of Breitbart Jerusalem. Donald Trump later appointed former Breitbart chair Stephen Bannon as his chief strategist in November 2016, a separate political connection between the network and Trump’s administration. The supplied reporting does not show that Trump launched or directed Breitbart Jerusalem. The entry’s January 2007 date and claim that the Israeli site began then conflict with the timeline in the JTA account. The two events—the trip when the founders discussed a media company and the later launch of an Israel-focused publication—should be dated separately.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Right-wing website Breitbart is launched in Israel
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Right-wing website Breitbart is launched in Israel

notes: Needs context: JTA dates Breitbart Jerusalem’s launch to November 2015 and describes 2007 as the trip when Solov and Andrew Breitbart discussed the parent network. Proposed correction: distinguish the 2007 trip from the 2015 site launch and remove the unsupported 2007 launch date.

title: Trump: 2010s Overview: Economic collapse, Russian investments, Fox News, elections change
description_short: Trump: 2010s Overview: Economic collapse, Russian investments, Fox News, elections change
description_medium: The linked Trump File page combines claims about shopping-mall closures, Russian investment, Fox News coverage and changes in election results across the 2010s. It gives no dated figures or supporting citations for these separate topics and does not identify a specific Trump action connecting them. The material is too broad to support a single factual account of election interference.

preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: 2010s Overview: Economic collapse, Russian investments, Fox News, elections change

title: Donald Trump uses Trump Foundation to bribe Florida Attorney General
description_short: Donald Trump uses Trump Foundation to bribe Florida Attorney General
description_medium: The Trump Foundation paid $25,000 in 2013 to a political group connected to Florida Attorney General Pam Bondi while her office was considering Trump University complaints. The Foundation later reported the payment as an illegal political contribution, corrected its filing, paid a penalty and reimbursed the money. The available account does not establish an agreement exchanging the donation for official action.
description_long: A 2016 Washington Post report said the Donald J. Trump Foundation paid $25,000 in 2013 to a political group connected to Florida Attorney General Pam Bondi while her office was considering fraud allegations involving Trump University. The Foundation initially reported the payment as a donation to a Kansas charity with a similar name; that charity did not receive the money. The Foundation later corrected its tax filing, paid a $2,500 penalty and reimbursed the Foundation, according to a Trump Organization official. The Foundation acknowledged that the payment was an illegal political contribution. Bondi’s office did not pursue the Trump University matter. These facts document a prohibited contribution and its timing in relation to the office’s consideration of complaints. They do not show that Trump paid Bondi personally, that she agreed to a quid pro quo or that the donation caused her office’s decision. The word “bribe” asserts an exchange that the available account does not establish; the supported description is an illegal political contribution followed by a correction and penalty.

preserved_fields.title: Donald Trump uses Trump Foundation to bribe Florida Attorney General
preserved_fields.description_short: Donald Trump uses Trump Foundation to bribe Florida Attorney General

notes: Needs context: the sources support an illegal political contribution, filing correction and penalty, but not an agreement exchanging the payment for official action. Proposed correction: use “illegal political contribution” unless evidence establishes bribery.

title: Donald Trump gives out Sen. Lindsey Graham's personal cell number
description_short: Donald Trump gives out Sen. Lindsey Graham's personal cell number
description_medium: At a campaign appearance on July 21, 2015, Donald Trump displayed a paper bearing Senator Lindsey Graham’s personal phone number and read it aloud. The disclosure took place during their public political dispute after Graham criticized Trump’s candidacy. Graham later said he changed his number. The linked account does not report physical injury or a criminal case arising from the incident.
description_long: During a campaign appearance on July 21, 2015, Donald Trump held up a piece of paper with Senator Lindsey Graham’s personal phone number and read it aloud to the crowd and cameras. The linked account places the disclosure amid their political dispute after Graham criticized Trump’s presidential candidacy. Graham later said he changed his phone number. He continued to criticize Trump after the event, including questioning his readiness to handle military and foreign-policy matters, so the disclosure did not end their disagreement. The immediate consequence reported was a change to Graham’s contact arrangements. Publishing private contact details can expose someone to unwanted calls and messages, but the source does not quantify what Graham received or report a resulting physical injury, criminal charge or court ruling. The documented event is the public disclosure of a senator’s personal number during a campaign dispute, followed by his changing it.

preserved_fields.title: Donald Trump gives out Sen. Lindsey Graham's personal cell number
preserved_fields.description_short: Donald Trump gives out Sen. Lindsey Graham's personal cell number

notes: The account documents Trump’s disclosure and Graham’s subsequent number change; it does not report injury, prosecution or a court ruling.
